title: Flat affine base change of global Hom out of a perfect space complex
statement:
Use schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces with their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ for the full subcategory with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Derived pushforward is computed by K-injective resolutions and tensor pullback $Lh^*$ by K-flat resolutions. Quasi-compact means that every open cover has a finite subcover; quasi-separated means the diagonal is quasi-compact. A perfect complex is etale locally isomorphic to a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free structure-sheaf modules. Write $R\operatorname{Hom}_Z(P,Q)=R\Gamma(Z,R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_Z}(P,Q))$ for global derived Hom, where internal Hom is [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and $R\Gamma$ is the right derived global-sections functor. If $Z$ is over $\operatorname{Spec}A$, regard this as an object of $D(A)$ by restriction of scalars. Its degree-$j$ cohomology is canonically $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_Z)}(P,Q[j])$. Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $Y'=\operatorname{Spec}B$, and $g:Y'\to Y$ its spectrum morphism. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a flat morphism, with $X$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space; flatness is tested on etale scheme charts. Form $X'=X\times_Y Y'$ with projections $h:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$. For every perfect $P\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ and every $Q\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$, the canonical map
$$c_{P,Q}:R\operatorname{Hom}_X(P,Q)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_{X'}(Lh^*P,Lh^*Q)$$
is an isomorphism in $D(B)$. It is natural in both arguments. The map is the $B$-linear extension, under derived extension/restriction of scalars, of the $A$-linear pullback-induced map of global Hom complexes. Under the unit $H\to\operatorname{Res}(H\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B)$ its underlying map is precisely that pullback-induced map. No boundedness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Put $E=R\mathcal Hom_X(P,Q)$. The perfect case of [lem-sfb-space-pseudocoherent-rhom-quasicoherent] gives $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$. Since $Y$ is affine it is quasi-separated, so [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence] makes $f$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated from the hypotheses on $X$. Thus the flat pushforward base-change theorem applies to $f$ and $E$.

proof.text: Regard $h$ as its canonical ringed-topos morphism using [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]. The evaluation-normalized comparison of [lem-sfb-ringed-perfect-internal-hom-pullback] gives an isomorphism $\alpha:Lh^*E\to R\mathcal Hom_{X'}(Lh^*P,Lh^*Q)$, natural in $P,Q$. Only $P$ is required perfect; $Q$ remains unbounded.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-flat-space-derived-pushforward-base-change], $\beta_E:Lg^*Rf_*E\to Rf'_*Lh^*E$ is invertible and $F=Rf_*E$ has quasi-coherent cohomology. For an affine scheme $Z$, write $G_Z=R\Gamma(Z,-)$. Apply [lem-sc-mixed-extension-sections-unit] on the Zariski sites to $R\epsilon_{Y,*}F$. Transport along [lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence], whose equivalence unit/counit and pullback comparisons preserve the scalar-insertion maps. This gives $s:G_Y(F)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B\simeq G_{Y'}(Lg^*F)$ with $U(s)\circ\eta^T=\sigma\circ G_Y(\eta^g_F)$; $U$ is scalar restriction and $\sigma$ is derived sections/direct-image composition. No boundedness or flatness of $g$ is required. Applying $G_{Y'}$ to $\beta_E$ gives an isomorphism $d:R\Gamma(X,E)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B\to R\Gamma(X',Lh^*E)$, using [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] for $f,f'$ followed by their maps to the one-point ringed topoi. Both equivalences use the actual derived global sections. The naturality of these identifications is part of the cited statements.

proof.text: Postcompose $d$ with $R\Gamma(X',\alpha)$ to obtain an isomorphism $\Theta$ with the required endpoints. Its scalar-extension adjoint is the geometric pullback map: the unit equation for $s$ above gives $G_Y(\eta^g_F)$ followed by $G_{Y'}(\beta_E)$ and the composition comparisons. The mate $\beta_E$ is adjoint to $Lf'^*Lg^*Rf_*E\simeq Lh^*Lf^*Rf_*E\xrightarrow{Lh^*\epsilon^f_E}Lh^*E$. Substitute this formula: naturality moves $\eta^f$ past $\eta^g$, and $Rf_*\epsilon^f\circ\eta^fRf_*=1$ cancels the adjacent unit and counit. The remaining arrow is $R\Gamma(X,E)\to R\Gamma(X',Lh^*E)$ induced by $\eta^h_E$. This is mate pasting [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], with the adjunction-compatible composition comparisons of [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus]. Postcomposing with $\alpha$ gives exactly global-Hom pullback, by its pulled-back evaluation formula. Thus $U(\Theta)\eta^T$ is the stated pullback-induced map. The extension/restriction adjunction gives a unique $B$-linear extension, so $\Theta=c_{P,Q}$. All factors are natural in both variables.
